title: Seepage
haiku:
Ghost rain through the ice
a lifetime of patient pipe
one neutrino caught
headline: Francis Halzen won the Nobel Prize in Physics for his decades of work detecting high-energy neutrinos from space using the IceCube observatory buried in Antarctic ice.

title: Undercurrent
haiku:
Wires we never see
carry feeling cell to cell
old plumber nods, pleased
headline: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discoveries showing how nerve cells shape human feelings.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Streets fill like a drain
backed up rent they can't afford
Madrid finds its voice
headline: Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across Spain to protest the country's housing crisis.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Red pipe, blue water
finds a crack in the old main
I smell the spring thaw
headline: New polling shows Senate races in Republican-leaning states trending toward Democratic candidates.

title: Leakproof
haiku:
He hid them from war
grown grey, they embrace him now
the pipe still holds true
headline: An elderly man was reunited with the children he saved from Nazi occupation decades ago, in a moment arranged by Esther Rantzen.

title: Outflow
haiku:
Twenty-three years drain
the last convoy leaves Iraq
pipes we built remain
headline: After 23 years, the last American forces have withdrawn from Iraq, leaving the country's future uncertain.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Storm drains gasp, then flood
I sized these pipes for less rain
the sky forgot code
headline: A powerful nor'easter caused flooding across the northeastern US, prompting New York and New Jersey to declare states of emergency.

title: Unscheduled
haiku:
A clock stopped its count
on death row, then someone signed
and let her walk free
headline: Mary Jane Veloso, once sentenced to death for drug trafficking, was granted a pardon and freed.

title: Backflow
haiku:
I've heard threats like these
yet the line still carries talk
old pipes, still some flow

title: Backflow
haiku:
Newsrooms shut the valve,
one signal, all outlets balk,
clean water still runs.

title: Discovery
haiku:
Old pipes hold no lies
a judge opens the sluice gate
truth finally flows
headline: A federal judge ordered Fox News to turn over hundreds of documents in a shareholder lawsuit over its election-fraud coverage.

title: Relief
haiku:
One valve turned by hand
Seoul says no more troops abroad
pressure finds its ease

title: Tributary
haiku:
Old allies reroute
round a wall no one can name
water finds its way

title: Leverage
haiku:
One valve, one desert
turns the whole world's pressure gauge
I taught men to flow
headline: Saudi Arabia shut a major oil pipeline after a drone attack launched from Iraq, part of the escalating standoff between Iran and the U.S.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve held its line
someone tried to brew plague code
and the pipe held fast

title: Shortfall
haiku:
Far right rises, short
one seat from the flood gate's edge
still the old seal holds

title: Loaner
haiku:
A borrowed kidney
keeps filtering past the odds
the system still flows

title: Undammed
haiku:
Born here, still it flows
a judge holds the old pipe true
bedrock outlasts men
headline: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration's second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship.

haiku:
Nepal's rivers rose
and swallowed a sleeping town
I have seen this rise
headline: Nepal's flash floods swept away a town, rescuers pulled survivors from a hydropower tunnel, and officials warned a glacial lake could breach and flood again.

haiku:
Ceuta's channel bends
a valve turned, the young let through
water finds the sea
headline: Spain reversed policy to allow 500 migrant children stranded in Ceuta to relocate to the mainland.

haiku:
My own blood, retooled,
learns to filter what returns—
old pipes, new gasket.
headline: A new personalized cancer vaccine trial showed it can prevent the disease from returning.

haiku:
Small lungs, once clogged pipes,
we scrubbed the air and they cleared
I've seen pipes heal too.

title: Bedrock
haiku:
Foundations were poured
a judge rules the blueprints hold
no whim moves concrete

title: Reflow
haiku:
Nine months in the pipe
the blockage clears, he walks out
water finds its way

title: Aftershock

Ground gave no warning
and swallowed a hundred homes
I light one candle
headline: A powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, killing well over a hundred people as rescuers search the rubble for survivors.

haiku:
The ground stopped holding
and the roofs came down like rain
we dig by hand now

title: Setback
haiku:
Another blueprint
shelved before the concrete dries—
still, I mix more sand

title: Backflow
haiku:
One valve did not break
though the current pushed, it held
clean water still flows

title: Opener
haiku:
Women take the field
history swings open wide
a door long rusted

title: Unthrottled
haiku:
Missouri said no
to narrowing their own valve
the pipe stays open

title: Rounds
haiku:
No duct cools this flat,
so the mailman checks the pulse—
old pipes, older hearts.
headline: As a heat wave strains France's elderly, postal workers have taken to checking on isolated seniors during their daily rounds.

title: Reflow
haiku:
A valve turned back on
vaccines flow to children's arms
the pipe remembers
headline: The U.S. restored some vaccine and health aid funding to UNICEF, Gavi, and the World Food Programme.

title: Spillway
haiku:
Rivers seek new banks
one skirmish floods a region
I've seen this spillway
headline: The U.S. launched fresh strikes on Iran, widening the war as it draws in Iraqi militias and other regional actors.

haiku:
Two days, no new strike
some valve somewhere holds the line
and the crude runs calm

haiku:
Target the water
and the bridge that lifts the light
the grid always mends

title: Satirical

a joke finds its spine
millions laughing turn to march—
the street clears its throat

title: Removable
haiku:
no tanks in the street —
a moving van at Downing,
keys change hands by vote

I taught men to build
bridges, pipelines, waterworks —
how quickly boys break

haiku:
the sweepers come out
as they did in every war —
brooms outlast bombers

fences do come down —
I have lived long enough, twice,
to watch walls give up

haiku:
I outlive them all —
men I argued with for years
the flag still half-mast

haiku:
sons avenging sons —
the oldest sewage on earth
still flows down to us

drones don't have mothers —
that's the engineering point —
someone's son still does

the summit's group shot:
smiles rowed up like clean fenceposts
smoke behind the lens

two hundred fifty —
the oath still means what it says
even when we don't

title: Splashdown

the kids in fountains
don't know they're a data point —
let them have the splash

we warmed the whole sea —
my grandchildren swim in it —
we can cool it too

the court holds the line:
born here is born here. full stop.
some days we're still us

five days under stone
and the street still claps for one —
that's the whole species

tit, then tat, then tit —
I flunked students for logic
looped as bad as this

the small island wins —
somewhere the odds-makers weep
good. let them. dance on

eleven thousand
hands that move the world's breakfast
wait on famous men

neighbors, not governments, dig
first, and bare-handed

he resigns, and goes —
power handed over like
a borrowed garden

thirty-two names read —
the olive trees keep standing
as we keep falling

I believe it like springtime:
briefly, completely

the strait opens wide —
gulls escort the tankers home
see? we can fix things

in a locked-down year,
we still reached the rusted plains,
hope wearing a mask

a sleeve rolled at dawn,
the whole locked world leaned in close—
one small needle's prick

a ring of fire round the dark—
the void has a face

flood waters rising—
divers thread the flooded dark,
twelve boys breathe again

the ball dropped, the town exhaled,
next year has arrived

the ripple crossed a billion
years to chime on earth

love need not ask permission
now, the rings went on

twenty four miles of falling—
the sky held its breath

seven minutes, dark,
cables lowered a robot,
Mars held its red breath

a shy field gave the world its
weight—we clapped like fools

she tore off her shirt and screamed,
a sport had arrived

one cell learned a trick
and grew into wool and legs—
the flock gained a twin

he took the oath as free man
a nation stood tall

a train now slides beneath waves,
England meets France now

one man strung a thread
through each door around the world
and called it open

we built an eye and
flung it past the atmosphere,
to watch time unfold

a wish in glass dish
grew into a girl who cried—
time—and she woke thin

we pressed our whole world
onto gold, and let it fly,
past the edge of home

the lights went to black
yellow words climbed into stars,
and we all believed

bones in the dry wash
the radio sang her name
grandmother, hello

a piano sighs,
no heaven, no hell, just us,
the world holds its breath

the wire failed at two letters
lo, the world began

half a million found the same
chord in the same rain

we watched in gray light,
a man stepped onto the moon—
the whole earth held still

cold wind, borrowed amps,
London looked up from its lunch,
the roof was the stage

four lads in mustache—
a marching band full of dreams,
the needle drops now

haiku:
fifteen minutes up,
a splash, a sailor's salute,
and the free world cheered

down past all sunlight,
seven miles of patient dark—
two men touched the floor

a beach-ball of steel
beeped once round the sleeping earth—
and nobody slept

the paint wasn't dry,
still, children ran through a dream,
the gates stayed open

a needle ends the long dread,
children swim again

two men cut the last
few steps to the roof of earth—
and stood in thin air

two strands climbed and twined,
the code of us laid bare in
one photograph's light

the world, still bleeding,
wrote down what a person's owed—
ink dried into law

and the whole league held its breath,
then he stole for all

we strung two towers, rust-red,
and walked clean across

he ran, and the lies—
four golds in the tyrant's yard,
the crowd roared for him

one engine, one girl,
the ocean had no vote here—
Ireland met her wheels

hard times, hungry streets—
still we raised a spire of steel,
the sky gained a floor

a farm boy blinked twice
between two star-crowded plates—
one small dot had moved

a mouse whistled once,
sound and ink shook hands and grinned,
the dark room laughed loud

one man, one thin plane
crossed an ocean, wide awake—
Paris met the dawn

a candle, a crack
gold glinted back through the dust
he breathed: wonders, yes

the wasting child slept,
a needle full of borrowed
time—and she woke thin

one state, then the vote—
the ballot box learned her name,
a signature, cast

the sun bent starlight,
and a patent clerk's wild guess
became the whole sky

two seas never touched—
we cut the waist of the world,
ships walk uphill now

clouds hid a city
stone stairs climbing to nowhere
the world looked up, up

she boiled tons of ore
to find a pinch that glowed blue—
night forgot to fall

a stunt, they all said—
iron lace against gray sky,
it forgot to fall

you press the button
the rest, he said, is our job
now the moment stays

a thread of carbon
burned through the night, refusing
to blink or give in

a needle traced tin
and gave the man his own voice
back to his own ear

come here, Watson, please—
a copper wire carried voice
and the world leaned in

no fence, no owner
the geysers belong to all
we saved it for us

two rails reached for hands
a golden spike rang them shut
the coasts shook hands, done

haiku:
December frost bites—
last chains hit the courthouse floor—
free, at last, by law

the new year turned once—
a signature broke the chains,
men woke up as men

all creatures, it turns
share one long and branching root—
we're kin to the moss

they aimed a pencil
at one dark spot in the sky—
and found a planet

he could not hear it—
joy poured from a silent man,
the hall wept and clapped

a farm boy's cowpox,
one scratch, and the pox lost teeth—
we named it vaccine

four small lights in line
swung round Jupiter each night—
the earth lost its throne
